countingRule: 21 implementation tickets T01-T21, excluding the parent specification issue; each produced target has exactly one carrier; consumer integrations are not second producers

tickets.title: Establish WebUI migration conformance and role-aware prefactoring gates
tickets.delivers: Developers can start the migration with reproducible behavior baselines and checks that recognize the accepted business/role homes without accepting duplicate ownership.
acceptance: Pin the product baseline and inventory canonical resources, public commands and existing verification seams; classify the accepted correction ledger separately from structural equivalence.
Restore command-surface generation against the actual source home without changing published command meaning or frozen protocol expectations; reproduce the existing ENOENT before repair.

Expand role/public-private import checks to recognize target homes alongside current homes; reject private peer imports, presentation business IO/writer construction and conversation imports of feature implementation.
Prove check sensitivity with legal and illegal dependency/call fixtures, including type-only imports and callable props, without adding blanket exemptions or new baseline violations.
Run representative current application, wire and browser baseline scenarios and record actual PASS/FAIL/unrun boundaries; no production ownership migration occurs in this prefactoring ticket.
Register required test/generator inputs and source inventory; publish the baseline ledger for downstream tickets and leave the applicable prefactoring gates green.
tickets.verification: Existing dependency-rule/tool tests plus public application/stream/protocol/browser baseline scenarios; deliberately illegal fixtures prove the role check can fail.
tickets.nonGoals: No feature refactor, product behavior redesign, frozen-oracle edit or suppression of an existing failing gate.

tickets.title: Boot and dispose one explicitly assembled WebUI application
tickets.delivers: Real browser boot and offline fixtures use one dormant assembly with correct selected-session unread hydration, one ingress and explicit cleanup.
acceptance: Construct owners without IO; start receives initial selection, hydrates persisted state before the first unread write, installs existing authoritative handlers and opens one event ingress.
Production, standalone preview and SSR fixtures use the same assembly; SSR starts no IO and required production wiring absence fails clearly.
Enforce constructed-to-started-to-disposed lifecycle, idempotent start/dispose, fresh epochs for fresh instances and refusal to restart a disposed store.
Remove the shell's alternate application factory and root storage divergence without duplicating live stores, subscriptions or authority.
Exercise actual root assembly inputs, remount/replay and selected-session storage traces; timers and ingress stop at disposal and late callbacks cannot commit.

Produce the opaque credential/config epoch context and public invalidation contract used by all owners; successful Account/Models/Settings commands and authoritative runtime reconciliation advance their applicable epochs without exposing credential values.

Assemble existing real workspace, history, queue and other business owners behind narrow application commands, exposing required reconciliation adapters before T05. These are real paths, not no-op placeholders or new copies of owner policy; existing event semantics remain single-path until T05 replaces them atomically.
tickets.verification: Public assembled lifecycle with injected storage/channel plus built-client boot/remount and real loopback startup/shutdown.
tickets.nonGoals: Does not install T05 domain policy or redefine Composer resets.

tickets.title: Fence keyed queries through one Models owner and model selection path
tickets.delivers: Model catalogues and selection remain correct across slow responses, session/provider changes and invalidation, with one business owner consumed by model presentation.
acceptance: Provide explicit resource-keyed and selected-slot contracts; commit checks owner incarnation, request generation and selected identity where appropriate.
Coalesce only equal response-affecting key/freshness/incarnation reads; invalidation cannot join an obsolete request as a completed repair.
Key model answers by global versus session/agent context and opaque credential/config generations; provider changes invalidate affected answers and status owners through published commands.
Models public commands/read models own catalogue, provider CRUD/test/discovery and selection; preserve supported favorite, variant, focus and draft-preview behavior.
Move model grouping/key/focus rules and coherent menu/draft editor UI into Models' target home; do not split individual hover callbacks mechanically.
Reproduce late A overwriting selected B on the old seam, then prove keyed independence, selected-slot suppression, freshness coverage and disposed-owner rejection through public commands.
tickets.verification: Assembled Models commands/read models with adversarial capabilities plus model keyboard/focus/provider browser scenarios.
tickets.nonGoals: The common primitive owns mechanics only; no global business cache or duplicate Composer model owner remains in the final programme.

tickets.title: Run headless turn delivery with retained scopes and coherent home adoption
tickets.delivers: Send, attach, retry and stop work through the application's conversation API even when the initiating React surface changes or disappears.
acceptance: Move writer/sink construction and send/attach/retry/stop orchestration into bounded conversation commands, leaving React bindings as subscriptions and invocations.
Separate selected, secondary, delivery and settlement leases; selection release cannot abandon accepted attempts or invalidation obligations, and eligible work prevents owner/fence recreation.
Preserve generation/cursor/resume-overflow/refusal settlement semantics; superseded attempts cannot write or release a newer lease.
Coordinate home record, writer identity, selected session and draft/history adoption with batched notifications and no intermediate mixed identity.
Track actual independent stream disposers; disposal/detach closes client delivery and fences callbacks without implicitly aborting harness execution.
Test headless/public send, attach, retry, explicit stop, navigation during accepted work, successful adoption and purge tombstones with non-empty delivery traces.
tickets.verification: Assembled conversation command/stream traces, existing lease/recovery tests and real loopback send/resume/detach/stop paths.
tickets.nonGoals: No goal/provider/workspace policy in conversation and no all-session automatic attachment.

tickets.title: Commit and reconcile goals and interactions through permanent application routes
tickets.delivers: Recognized session facts and matching permission/questionnaire/goal operations update the right owners without requiring a mounted Composer.
acceptance: Install permanent owner routes before ingress; remove UI-populated effects registry and whole-set effect replacement in the same atomic ownership transfer.
Goal and interaction owners have independent session-keyed fences and narrow writers; all facts, reads and accepted command outcomes use their owner commit path.
Recognized data events for valid non-purged identities commit while unmounted; inactive read-required resources remain dirty and interested scopes reconcile on selection/reconnect.
Keep acknowledgement as acceptance rather than a subscription barrier; test events before/after ready and reconnect gaps without duplicate subscriptions or owner writes.
Preserve request-specific permission/questionnaire settlement, goal CRUD/steering and ordered progress effects; reset goal input presentation without clearing retained goal truth.

Remove goal/interaction factory construction and business handler registration from Composer; move their binding/UI responsibilities to the target businesses and publish interfaces for Composer/Transcript.

Permanent routes call T02's real application-owned workspace/history/queue reconciliation commands through explicit temporary adapters; later carriers replace that owner's implementation without installing a second route or writer. No missing route is hidden by a no-op.
Reproduce the empty-registry goal commit gap and verify accepted compatibility spellings plus actual emitter integration, stale responses, dirty coverage and tombstone behavior.
tickets.verification: Assembled installed event ingress and goal/interaction commands; real loopback emitter/reconnect paths and goal/questionnaire browser behavior.
tickets.nonGoals: No generic internal event bus, background fetch fan-out or new interaction UX.

tickets.title: Unify canonical history, context reads and transcript live handoff
tickets.delivers: History pagination, live/settled display, context usage and feedback remain coherent through one canonical history interface without duplicate messages or conflicting readers.
acceptance: Replace singleton selected-session request ownership with keyed session/page history and separately fenced selected presentation.
Preserve older-page merge, context snapshot precedence, cursor recovery and one rendering source per turn; compatible context inspection joins the correct owner read.
Do not conflate pagination anchors, stream recovery or differing result coverage merely to deduplicate requests.
Transcript owns grouping/view projection, scroll binding and feedback commands; compose public interaction/review surfaces without importing their private writers or implementing their query policy.
Move transcript contracts/projections/bindings/UI to its target home and history rules to conversation; cut the large transcript by coherent view-model, scroll and response responsibilities.
Verify fast session switches, overlapping page/context readers, accepted goal-message events, feedback errors, live-to-history handoff and non-empty message counts.
tickets.verification: Assembled history/transcript outcomes plus frozen message/turn fixtures and built-browser scrolling/live handoff.
tickets.nonGoals: Turn/workspace review query ownership is produced by T10, not copied here.

tickets.title: Own session catalogue, rail overlays and lifecycle commands in Sessions
tickets.delivers: Session rail, archived settings and import/export entry surfaces use one Sessions owner whose successful mutations update every relevant view and purge deleted state coherently.
acceptance: Own flat/tree/project catalogue, activity/unread and browser rail overlays; one entity update feeds both catalogue query views.
Expose create/select/archive/fork/rename/import/export/delete commands and availability/outcomes; settings and shell invoke them instead of owning alternate paths.
Successful delete coordinates record/draft/query/interest purge and tombstones; failed deletion retains state and accepted late work cannot resurrect the ID.
Consume T04 home-adoption transaction rather than producing a second transaction; retain storage keys/formats/normalization/pruning and selected-session unread semantics.
Move rail grouping/filtering/activity rules and cohesive project expansion/list/row/menu units into Sessions; preserve menus, search, pins/stars, pagination and transfer behavior.
Verify public mutation/read-model traces and real rail/archive/import/export browser entry paths, including hidden surfaces and session switches.
tickets.verification: Assembled Sessions commands/read models, transfer loopback integration and rail browser menu/search/overlay scenarios.
tickets.nonGoals: No second catalogue/session store, product reclassification of projects or hidden default workspace changes.

tickets.title: Serve plugin management and Composer catalogues through typed Plugins ownership
tickets.delivers: Marketplace, installed plugins, skills, MCP and agent forms plus Composer catalogue readers use typed named intents and independent correct resource queries.
acceptance: Cover the complete existing plugin-management action union, validator action set and input-shape population with a typed internal action/result adapter; preserve the wire operation and accepted behavior.

Separate catalogue-selection, detail, installed-plugin and runtime-skill identities including session/agent/workspace context where applicable; management and mention readers cannot overwrite each other.
Publish named listing/detail/mutation commands and Composer-facing installed-plugin/runtime-skill read models; no caller must dispatch an arbitrary wire action string.
Split the large catalogue into cohesive catalogue composition and MCP/agent/skill/import form units; local form drafts stay local and mutation errors remain distinct from availability.
Move Plugins implementation to its business home, preserving reload/filter/preview/import/install/enable/delete/agent-chat behavior and targeted mutation invalidation.
Parse the three authoritative action populations and prove exhaustive non-duplicated coverage; test stale detail/list requests and catalogue/form/mention consumer outcomes.
tickets.verification: Assembled Plugins commands with actual internal adapters, server validator/wire compatibility and catalogue/MCP/browser consumers.
tickets.nonGoals: No new plugin action, service, unrestricted dispatch or copied Composer catalogue query.

tickets.title: Make browser account status and login follow one Account lifetime
tickets.delivers: Account login, status, check-in, sign-out and Composer credential-status readers agree across account/session switches while polling and stale callbacks clean up correctly.
acceptance: Use one application-owned Account workflow with attempt/credential/config epochs and public account/API-key/OAuth credential-status, quota/login/check-in/sign-out commands and availability; migrate credential-status reads currently owned by Settings rather than create another copy.
Move polling and request truth out of presentation; hidden/remounted consumers acquire appropriate interest without duplicating owner state or timers.
Sign-out/switch invalidates obsolete status and model-dependent answers through public collaboration and preserves real revoke/wipe runtime semantics.
Keep tokens/auth leases/refresh ownership runtime-side; browser query keys use opaque generations, never credential values.
Preserve signed-out, unavailable, failure/retry and accepted quota degradation branches; failed mutation does not pretend success.
Move account contracts/projections/bindings/UI together and test pending login, late account response, session switch and disposal through public seams and account browser fixtures.
tickets.verification: Assembled Account capability/storage/timer traces and browser account/login/status scenarios; real cloud acceptance separately labeled.
tickets.nonGoals: Runtime quota adapter/projection extraction is produced by T17; no new credential behavior.

tickets.title: Own turn changesets and workspace snapshots through distinct Review APIs
tickets.delivers: Transcript diff cards and workspace review share authoritative query/mutation ownership while turn changeset and working-tree snapshot identities stay distinct.
acceptance: Own turn diff queries/revert/reapply and workspace summary/file-diff/search in separate resource families; preserve snapshot mismatch handling and bounded stale-snapshot retry.
Remove DiffCard-owned IO/query truth and extract only the review responsibility from the mixed workspace query owner; T11 owns files/environment responsibility.
Turn mutations invalidate the affected turn and workspace families as part of settlement; applicable external mutations mark affected turn resources dirty without global unrelated reloads.
Preserve unsupported versus mutation-failed outcomes and presentation expansion/search selection as local independent state.
Publish and integrate Review command/read APIs in both existing surfaces, with target business contracts/projections/bindings/UI and no schema identity substitution.
Test two simultaneous consumers, stale snapshots, failed and successful mutation outcomes and invalidation freshness through public APIs and visible review behavior.
tickets.verification: Assembled Review read/command traces, loopback mutation/snapshot paths and transcript/workspace review browser consumers.
tickets.nonGoals: No file/environment cache takeover, universal review snapshot or new Git mutation semantics.

tickets.title: Own workspace files, environment and panel use cases beyond React mounting
tickets.delivers: File/tree/environment/Git/canvas/preview/directory-browser behavior stays correct across workspace/tab switches through application owners and stable panel state.
acceptance: Extract files/tree/content and environment identities from the mixed query owner; compose T10 Review APIs rather than reimplementing review policy.
Workspace Git events directly invalidate matched environment/review owners without shell revision relay; preserve existing coalescing and unrelated-workspace isolation.
Own panel/tab state with existing session persistence semantics; tab close releases its interests and file/read commit rights without stopping unrelated accepted work.
Canvas/archive/preview/directory-browser commands have explicit outcome and freshness ownership; presentation performs DOM geometry/rendering only, with archive parsing produced by T16.
Move workspace contracts/projections/bindings/UI to its home and preserve file ranges/content/path, canvas gestures, media/HTML preview restrictions and error branches.
Test stale tab/file responses, inline-content supersession, workspace aliases, invalidation bursts and public panel actions plus real HTTP/file/Git paths and browser panel scenarios.
tickets.verification: Assembled workspace commands/query snapshots, HTTP range/content/path integration and panel/canvas/preview browser behavior.
tickets.nonGoals: T15 produces terminal ownership and T16 produces archive parser policy; this ticket only composes their existing/adopted public capabilities.

tickets.title: Own permission preferences and compose settings pages from their actual businesses
tickets.delivers: Instructions, memory, profile, permission preferences, providers, account and archived-session setting surfaces invoke the correct public business commands and coherent read models.
acceptance: Settings owns instruction/memory/profile policies and permission-preference reads/writes, exposes their named commands for Composer, and preserves its runtime-version read owner; Models, Account and Sessions own their own setting-page resources and credential-status queries.
Remove raw transport/function forwarding and private peer imports from settings presentation and shell wiring; inject or compose published read/command APIs.
Preserve existing read/write error, absence, normalization and runtime file/auth contracts; command failure cannot be returned as success.
Move settings contracts/projections/bindings/UI into its business home, including shared glyph relocation only through T18's generic presentation home.
Verify pending agent/profile changes, shared setting-page mutations and hidden/remount behavior through application outcomes and built-browser settings scenarios.
tickets.verification: Assembled Settings commands with actual peer public APIs, loopback personalization/profile paths and settings browser scenarios.
tickets.nonGoals: No duplicate models/account/archive owner, new preference or changed credential persistence.

tickets.title: Drive Composer submission, queue and editor through composed business owners
tickets.delivers: Ordinary sends, enqueues, commands, goals, attachments and mention/skill menus use one composed Composer workflow while all accepted field transitions and keyboard behavior remain.
acceptance: Consume published Sessions/Conversation/Goal/Interaction/Models/Plugins/Account/History and T12 Settings permission-preference commands; remove Composer's duplicate catalogue/status/context/preference RPC state.
Keep one application-owned active controller with the complete field transition matrix for selection/home adoption, hide/remount, accepted/successful/failed submit and disposal.
Fence the selected queue destination independently; retain session-gated retry, committed-intent input history, staging carryover and distinct goal/plan mode rules.
Own send/queue/goal/command orchestration and attachment/file-read outcomes outside rendering; runtime execution and visible sending/phase remain distinct.
Cut the large Composer into coherent editor/staging, toolbar, mention/slash/menu and transcript-placement presentation, with local caret/geometry/focus and no hook-per-state-variable fragmentation.
Verify all submission branches, current button/Enter shared gate, pending-selection results, goal reset/loading, seed deduplication, refusal/retry and queue failure without silently clearing input.
Move Composer roles to its business home and demonstrate the complete built-client input-to-owner-to-transport path with unchanged visible affordances.
tickets.verification: Assembled Composer intents/outcomes and actual owner collaborations plus composer keyboard/menu/attachment/queue/goal browser scenarios.
tickets.nonGoals: No new Composer reset UX, background attachment policy or peer owner recreation.

tickets.title: Bind loopback operations without redundant service forwarding
tickets.delivers: Clients still retrieve data and stream execution through the authenticated loopback server, with runtime methods bound once and semantic adapters retained.
acceptance: Inject a complete preassembled operation registry and runtime/terminal ports into the network service; delete identity-only forwarding closures without bypassing network ingress.

Produce the narrow terminal-process port consumed initially by the existing real terminal manager; T15 later migrates its implementation and service resource ownership behind that same port. Registry simplification does not wait for terminal relocation.
Keep typed shared binding machinery and explicit per-domain binding tables colocated with descriptors; preserve exhaustive operation completeness and deterministic registration/serialization.

Retain validators/allowlisting, exact optional-capability guards/errors, receiver binding, version projections, sign-out revoke/wipe, message/context projections and dedicated stream/terminal handlers.
Never select a runtime property by client input or enumerate runtime methods as exposed operations; no reflection or one-file-per-operation fragmentation.
Compare the complete existing operation population against frozen validator/frame/call/error/signal traces, including absent and non-callable capability cases.
Exercise actual loopback unary data retrieval, send/resume/events, terminal delivery and shutdown with the new assembled registry; no client-side access path disappears.
tickets.verification: Frozen wire and host-shape invariants plus real loopback request/stream/terminal lifecycle paths.
tickets.nonGoals: No public operation change, validator tightening, protocol topology change or removal of host adaptation.

tickets.title: Separate service-owned terminal processes from browser delivery and xterm attachments
tickets.delivers: Terminal creation/input/resize/watch and explicit disposal remain usable while hiding or closing a presentation attachment leaves the service-owned process intact.
acceptance: Move native process implementation into runtime with one manager per WebUI service resource scope; inject a terminal port into network registry/HTTP lifecycle rather than sharing a host-wide singleton.
Browser Terminal owner publishes catalogue/process commands and actual watch disposers; local xterm/fit/resize observers remain presentation bindings.
View release detaches watch/xterm only; explicit process disposal and service shutdown kill the proper PTYs with preserved teardown trace.
Cancellation finalizes listeners/parked iterators exactly once; test no-output waiting, exit, abort, detach and repeated disposal with visible resource traces.
Preserve process count limit, terminal identity, output/exited state and resize coalescing; no implicit session/tab-based process deletion is introduced.
Integrate workspace presentation against public Terminal API and exercise real native PTY create/write/resize/detach/dispose in the owning integration environment.
tickets.verification: Application terminal commands and loopback iterator cancellation plus real native PTY and xterm attachment behavior; fixtures and native evidence remain distinct.
tickets.nonGoals: No terminal protocol redesign, new process scope or kill-on-unmount behavior.

tickets.title: Modernize archive parsing behind preserved workspace preview and extraction policy
tickets.delivers: Supported workspace archive listing/extraction uses a mature parser adapter while preserving path, expansion, truncation and write-safety contracts visible to the user.
acceptance: Evaluate mature parser implementations against the existing supported format, entry/path/symlink, size/expansion and corruption contract; select and record a conforming dependency/license/version with evidence.
Keep parsing distinct from runtime path/expansion policy and listing/extraction workflows; no dependency-avoidance rationale justifies reimplementing mature formats.
Preserve recognized-but-unsupported outcomes, listing limits/truncation, prefix/destination behavior, exclusive/no-half-file writes and truthful partial extraction results.
Refactor the large archive module along parser/policy/workflow responsibility, integrating Workspace public commands without browser-side filesystem access.
Run real synthetic-file ZIP/TAR/gzip, unsafe-path/link/budget/corruption and partial-write conformance through the actual adapter/workflow, plus loopback preview/extraction consumers.
Fail explicitly if a required conformance case is unsupported; do not weaken safety tests, silently add formats or claim correctness from a stub parser.
tickets.verification: Actual chosen parser with filesystem conformance/security corpus, runtime archive workflows and loopback/browser archive consumer behavior.
tickets.nonGoals: No new archive feature or relaxed limits; parser selection is this ticket's executable work, not an unresolved operator question.

tickets.title: Separate quota requests and projections while retaining one runtime cache owner
tickets.delivers: Quota/check-in/account consumers retain their established signed-in, refresh, failure and degradation outcomes while cloud request and pure payload projection become maintainable seams.
acceptance: Keep one runtime quota/account identity/cache orchestration owner; extract coherent request and pure payload projection responsibilities only where the boundary hides real complexity.
Preserve identity keys, TTLs, in-flight sharing, force-refresh, signing, auth rejection/invalidation and accepted credits-only degradation.
Use the existing public result contract so browser Account does not need a parallel cache or credential owner.
Compare deterministic request/response/error/cache traces with the real imported implementation and assert clocks/identity changes, not only fixture values.
Exercise cloud acceptance only with authorized environment and report it separately; offline synthetic fetch outcomes prove their declared seam only.
Record a coherent keep decision for portions of the large module that remain one responsibility; do not split each endpoint into a service.
tickets.verification: Runtime quota public outcomes with controlled real adapter/clock traces; optional live endpoint acceptance clearly separated.
tickets.nonGoals: No TTL/degradation/product pricing change, browser token persistence or generic global cache.

tickets.title: Migrate remaining browser IO and generic presentation mechanics to their target homes
tickets.delivers: Completed businesses obtain IO through injected platform adapters and reusable presentation through a generic UI home, with no alternate technical-root homes left for those populations.
acceptance: Use the role expansion from T01, then mechanically migrate only platform IO and genuinely generic UI/binding populations not produced by earlier business tickets.

Separate wire lifecycle mechanics from domain method tables using canonical operation identifiers; preserve unary deadlines, finite stream completion/errors, event reconnect and terminal-watch behavior.
Keep browser storage/DOM/file/download adapters injected, with identical keys/normalization and no platform import of application or business implementation.
Generic glyph/markdown/math/overlay/subscription mechanics contain no business policy; feature bindings produced by their carriers are consumed, not moved a second time.
Compare moved bodies with AST-aware equivalence and exercise built consumer paths; no stale imports, compatibility re-export shims, duplicated writer or per-feature transport instance remains.
Update source inventory/build inputs and role/public API checks for the exact migrated population; publish the remaining-population census for T21 contract retirement.
tickets.verification: Expand-migrate-contract wide-refactor batch with moved-body equivalence, dependency/build checks and existing wire/storage/UI consumer scenarios.
tickets.nonGoals: No second ownership migration for businesses, new generic bus/cache or changed socket topology.

tickets.title: Finish the WebUI shell as layout and public business composition
tickets.delivers: The shell displays rail, Composer, settings, catalogue and workspace through public business APIs while owning only layout/visibility/navigation presentation.
acceptance: Remove remaining business factories, canonical writes, raw capability relay, query truth, activity probes and workspace invalidation relay from shell; earlier carriers produce their replacement owners.
Compose named business screens/read models and owner commands; shell reactions subscribe after authoritative commits and cannot replace routes.
Keep UI-only menu/visibility/layout and injected navigation behavior; preserve plugin-surface hide/remount, memory handoff and session selection placement.
Cut the large foundation app into coherent layout/public composition without introducing another dependency container, service locator or shell business owner.
Move shell and its public presentation helpers to the target home; no consumer imports shell implementation for a business rule.
Verify complete browser screen switching, initial boot, pending turn while catalogue shown, rail/workspace placement and layout controls with zero shell-owned business RPC/writer call sites.
tickets.verification: Assembled public application plus built browser screen/navigation behavior and sensitive source call/import checks.
tickets.nonGoals: Does not recreate owners already delivered by prior tickets or redesign screens.

tickets.title: Co-locate feature styles while preserving the effective WebUI cascade
tickets.delivers: Styles follow their business or generic shell/UI owner without changing effective layout, responsive behavior or shared design-token authority.
acceptance: Classify the large shell stylesheet's rule populations by actual consumer ownership; global reset/layout/primitives remain global and feature rules follow their target business.
Retain one coherent shared token authority; a file-length threshold is not a reason to split token declarations.
Preserve stylesheet loading order, specificity, cascade, media queries and effective declarations; delete shadowed rules only after direct equivalence evidence.
Build the served client styles and compare computed styles plus representative real screenshots at existing responsive scenarios, including overlay/scroll/composer reserved space.
Run current browser interactions/accessibility selectors and record exact visual comparisons; raw CSS byte equality alone cannot establish parity.
tickets.verification: Built effective-style comparisons and real browser screenshots/geometry/interactions at pinned viewport/theme scenarios.
tickets.nonGoals: No visual redesign, new tokens/theme or numerical stylesheet line target.

tickets.title: Retire migration forms and verify the complete WebUI architecture contract
tickets.delivers: Developers can use the complete target architecture with authoritative documentation, no alternate owner homes and verified behavior across declared application, protocol and browser boundaries.
acceptance: Parse the board coverage and final source population: every target has one producing carrier, every accepted business has its public home, and every large-file responsibility has a completed cut or coherent keep decision.

Contract temporary old forms only after all consumers migrated; no compatibility re-export shims, stale source-tool mappings, duplicated complete stores, UI handler registries or generic capability hooks remain.
Finalize role/public API checks, package guide, command surface, business navigation, ADR/context links, source inventory, build inputs and suite registration to reflect the delivered tree.

Execute the complete applicable repository verifier on reviewed clean committed integration state, plus generated business navigation; fix covered failures without rewriting frozen oracles or suppressing gates.

Execute representative real loopback send/resume/event/terminal/file/transfer/shutdown and built-browser parity including screenshots, adversarial selection/epoch/invalidation and Composer field transitions.

Record offline, transport, native terminal, cloud, visual, performance and platform evidence distinctly; applicable performance/cross-platform requirements have actual receipts or clearly documented external gates.
Compare declared extension scenarios against the final public homes and report measured request/resource behavior without claiming improvement from plausible structure alone.
Update authoritative programme state and blockers from verified outputs; readiness of this ticket does not imply its dependent implementation work is already complete.
tickets.verification: Full declared integration verification and coverage/population audit; a green narrow gate cannot substitute for the complete acceptance scope.
tickets.nonGoals: No new eviction/flow-control/protocol design, reopened product scope or hidden implementation waiver.

partitionRule: The mixed workspace query file has two disjoint produced responsibilities: T10 produces review queries, T11 produces files/environment queries. Large-file carrier describes completion of its responsibility cut, not exclusive edits; all producing targets above remain unique. T19 consumes factories/state moved by prior business tickets rather than producing them again. T18 moves only the platform/generic UI residual population.

checks: distinct titles and contiguous T01-T21 ordinals
